inconsistencies: Chain: #35714 (stop writes after flush failure) is the base for #35731 (flush-error notification invariant); review #35714 first.
Chain: #35646 (separate runtime errors via util::Expected) explicitly unblocks #35570 (return BlockValidationState by value); review #35646 first.
Chain: #32575 (remove single-threaded script-check path) is stated groundwork for #29491 (Schnorr batch verification); review #32575 first.
Chain: #35861 (Testnet 5) is built on #35793 (BIP 54) and cannot be evaluated until BIP 54's rules are settled.

Overlapping problem: #34132, #35003, #36049 and #35714 all rework fatal I/O / database error handling in validation and block storage. #35003 carries an explicit Approach NACK on collapsing exceptions into nullable returns; a single decision on the exception-vs-status-return boundary should be made once and applied across all four, ideally starting from #35714/#34132.
Related pair: #35307 and #36346 both fix crashes that leave an assumeutxo node unbootable without reindex; they touch adjacent snapshot-activation paths and should be reviewed together.

Overlapping area: #33324 (reobfuscate existing block files) and #35938 (fail instead of writing a null XOR key) both change blocks/xor.dat handling; #35938 prevents data loss and should be reviewed first so #33324 can rely on its invariant.
Same project: #35906, #35569 and #36066 are all steps toward the stateless validation library (#35904); #35906 carries the testable payoff, #35569 and #36066 are mechanical prerequisites.

#35187 (kernel block validation without a UTXO set) drives a check-only ConnectBlock through a custom coins view, overlapping #36066's TestConnectBlock split; it is primarily a kernel-API PR and its validation-side change would benefit from being reviewed against #36066.
#35271 is motivated only by a downstream (Elements) chainstate layout and reviewers questioned whether Core is affected at all; it duplicates no merged work but has no demonstrated Core impact.
result.notes: The four regtest-only soft-fork implementations (#31989 CTV, #32247 CSFS, #29247 CAT, #35793 BIP 54, plus draft #36122 CISA) were banded as a group: none changes mainnet consensus, so their importance here is the cost of an unmade decision plus interpreter correctness. BIP 54 leads the group because it encodes fixes for known legacy consensus vulnerabilities. P1 is reserved for the four reproducible crash/corruption bugs in chainstate and assumeutxo handling.
